claim: The least cardinality of a finite \(T_0\)-space that is weakly contractible, noncontractible, and has trivial homeomorphism group is exactly \(10\). Among the ten classified ten-point beat-point-free examples, the unique rigid example is Type VII; this poset is self-dual and has exactly one order-reversing bijection, an involution. The homeomorphism groups of Types I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII are, respectively, \(C_2\), \(S_3\), \(C_2\times C_2\), \(C_2\times C_2\), \(C_2\), \(C_2\), and the trivial group; the order-duals of Types I--III have the same groups.
integrity_note: The graph-automorphism groups follow from cover-incidence relations in the cited classified models and an explicit exhaustive standalone permutation check.
limitations: Uniqueness among ten-point examples assumes beat-point-free; possibly nonminimal ten-point spaces are not classified.
Existing nine- and ten-point classification theorems and the recorded nine-point group C2 are cited prerequisites.
No original proof of contractibility or order complex collapse is claimed.
Literature search cannot guarantee exhaustive novelty.
scope: Finite T0 weakly contractible noncontractible spaces; full group classification only for ten-point beat-point-free members of the known ten-type list.
title: Ten points are necessary and sufficient for a rigid weakly contractible noncontractible finite space
